title: .NET 11 Preview 7 Brings Updates Across C#, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, and Windows Forms
gist: .NET 11 Preview 7 ships incremental language and framework updates: C# gains labeled break/continue and progresses union types, Blazor gets resource-saving circuit pausing and output caching, and EF Core, Windows Forms, MAUI and F# receive targeted improvements.

insights.claim: In C# under .NET 11 Preview 7, break and continue statements can name an enclosing loop or switch, letting code exit or continue an outer construct directly from an inner one without a flag or goto.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Reduces boilerplate control-flow hacks in nested loops, a small ergonomic win for C# developers.
insights.quote: the break and continue statements can now name an enclosing loop or switch, so code can leave or continue an outer construct directly from an inner one without a flag or a goto

insights.claim: Union types in C# remain a preview feature but now use a try-both approach that first tests a pattern against the union itself and then against its contained value, and switch-expression exhaustiveness understands generic parameters constrained to a closed type.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Signals Microsoft is steadily maturing discriminated-union-style patterns in C#, a long-requested feature.

themes.theme: ASP.NET Core and Blazor resource efficiency

insights.claim: Blazor Interactive Server circuits can now pause themselves when a browser tab is hidden, releasing server resources until the user returns, and a new CacheView component caches rendered output of a server-side subtree to cut processor and memory use.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Lowers server-side hosting costs for Blazor Server apps, addressing a known scalability pain point.
insights.quote: Interactive Server circuits can now pause themselves when a browser tab is hidden, releasing server resources until the user returns.

insights.claim: Preview 7 reverses part of Preview 6 so automatic cross-origin protection now validates only endpoints that opt in, matching .NET 10 behaviour so existing apps are not broken.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Shows Microsoft walking back a breaking default mid-preview, relevant for teams tracking upgrade risk.
insights.quote: automatic cross-origin protection now validates only endpoints that opt in, matching .NET 10 behaviour so existing apps are not broken

themes.theme: Data access and desktop framework updates

insights.claim: Entity Framework Core now translates int.Parse and related methods to a SQL Server CAST, rewrites several GroupBy patterns into single joins, adds the 16-bit Half type on SQLite, and modernises the Azure Cosmos DB provider to use System.Text.Json.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Incremental query-generation and provider improvements matter to teams optimizing EF Core data access.

insights.claim: Windows Forms introduces an opt-in modern rendering pipeline through VisualStylesMode, deferred form reveal to avoid an unstyled flash at startup, and a SuspendPainting scope that reduces flicker during bulk updates.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Microsoft continues investing in the legacy Windows Forms UI stack, signaling ongoing enterprise-desktop support.
